criteria.check: Read metrics.py compute(); every memo figure (M1-M16) is computed there. Compared float sums of M2/M9 against exact Decimal sums on all 10 committed statements: equal at 2dp, worst raw float error 3e-11.
Every Metric carries evidence ids (metrics.py:231-274). Separately, the CLI overwrites NAME.evidence.json on a later rejected run, and the Monzo importer drops Monzo's own transaction ids (findings).
draft node builds the prompt from as_table(metrics) and rules_table(policy) only; no transactions. A reused thread also feeds stale guard feedback from another statement's memo (see R4 finding).
Guard probes: 'A further 40 may be drawn' and a line starting '35. ' pass as grounded. Reusing --thread carries redrafts=2 and stale guard_feedback into a new statement's run.
review node interrupts until a valid ReviewDecision with reviewer; finalise only after review; --yes needs --reviewer and refuses ungrounded memos.
Ordered rule list, first match with direction wins; unmatched credit returns OTHER.
Policy is packaged YAML, validated (op, on_fail, when_missing, numeric thresholds) before evaluate.
Not in this seat's data lens; did not audit committed names or data provenance.

ingest.load_csv checks columns, extra fields, empty/duplicate ids, YYYY-MM-DD dates, future dates, plain 2dp amounts, date order (reverses newest-first) and the running balance chain; probes confirmed rejection. Float tolerance quirk is minor (finding).
CI runs ruff, pytest and evals with --llm fake, no secrets referenced; local pytest: 174 passed with no key.
Generated 675 statements (3 archetypes x 3 profiles x 25 seeds x {12m default end, 7m to 2024-03-31, 24m to 2026-02-28}); M2,M5,M6,M7,M8,M11,M12 (and M13,M15) all within 0.01 of truth; 0 mismatches.
guard.check on 'Revenue was £X [M2]. A further 40 may be drawn next quarter.' -> grounded True; same with a line '35. More covers next year.' -> grounded True. 40 is neither a date nor a list marker.

findings.claim: D4 is not fixed for cover: non-trading credits (director capital injection, transfer from savings, HMRC refund) are categorised OTHER and kept in `operating`, so they raise M9 and M10 (DSCR = (M9-M11)/M8) and R8. One £20k director injection turns a declining business from overall FAIL (DSCR 0.57x) into overall PASS (DSCR 1.68x); M16 is only 7.7% so R9 does not refer. categorise.py's own docstring says this is the outcome it prevents.
findings.repro: scratchpad/panel03/data-intensive/p3.py: 12 months of CARD SETTLEMENT 20000, supplier -18400, FINANCE LOAN -1500, OWNER DRAWINGS -500, 3 on-time HMRC VAT, vat_stagger=1. A_base: M9 16200, M10 0.57, R2 fail, overall fail. B_injection (+ 'FPS CREDIT DIRECTOR CAPITAL INJECTION' 20000 on 2026-03-03): M9 36200, M10 1.68, M16 7.7, all rules pass, overall pass.

findings.claim: M3 average monthly revenue divides revenue from the whole span (including the boundary months that covered_months drops) by the covered-month count, so it is overstated by up to ~28 days of takings. This is the figure lenders size facilities from.
findings.repro: scratchpad/panel03/data-intensive/p1_m3.py: CARD SETTLEMENT 1000/day from 2025-10-18 to 2026-10-14 -> M1 11, M2 362000, M3 32909.09; true average over the 11 covered months is 30363.64 (+8.4%).

findings.claim: M13 counts a VAT direct debit that was returned unpaid as a timely payment: the `paid` search ignores whether the debit was reversed (t.reverses links exist since D11). A bounced, never re-presented VAT payment gives M13 0 and R5 pass.
findings.repro: scratchpad/panel03/data-intensive/p3.py case C_vat_bounced: HMRC VAT DD -1000 on 2026-05-05, 'UNPAID DD HMRC VAT' +1000 on 2026-05-07, no re-presentment, stagger 1 -> M7 1, M12 2000 (correctly net), M13 0.0, R5 pass.

findings.claim: Same thread id twice is not idempotent: `load` does not reset per-run state, so re-running `cma run --thread X --checkpoint-db db` on another statement inherits redrafts=2 (no redraft budget left), the previous memo's guard_feedback (figures from a different statement sent to the model in the first draft) and the previous run's review and final_memo while the new memo awaits review.
findings.repro: scratchpad/panel03/data-intensive/p6_thread.py: run1 FakeLLM(hallucinate=True) on cafe_stretched thread 'acme', reject; run2 same thread on trades_good -> first prompt contains 'previous draft was rejected' and '48,250'; run2 redrafts 2; stale review present True; stale final_memo present True.

findings.claim: The evidence file name ignores the outcome: a rejected run with the same --out overwrites NAME.evidence.json, so the approved NAME.md is left paired with evidence for a different statement and a NOT-approved review.
findings.repro: scratchpad/panel03/data-intensive/p5_cli.py: run examples/cafe_stretched.csv --reviewer Alice --yes --out memo.md; then run evals/results/statements/trades_poor.csv --reviewer Bob --out memo.md, answer n -> memo.md still 'APPROVED by Alice', memo.evidence.json review approved False, reviewer Bob, statement trades_poor.csv.

findings.claim: The month-name date exemption accepts any 1-2 digit number followed by a month word, including days > 31 and the modal verb 'may' (IGNORECASE), so an ungrounded figure passes the guard. P2 allows only real dates.
findings.repro: guard.check('Revenue was £<M2> [M2]. A further 40 may be drawn next quarter.', metrics, policy) on examples/cafe_stretched.csv -> grounded True, unmatched [].

findings.claim: The Monzo importer builds descriptions from Type and Name only and drops Notes/Description, where the payment reference sits. No Monzo credit can carry an invoice reference, and processor payouts are not settlement-named, so every inflow becomes OTHER: M2 0, M3/M4 meaningless, M16 100%.
findings.repro: scratchpad/panel03/data-intensive/p7_monzo.py: 12 x Faster payment 'Oakfield Properties' 4000 with Description/Notes 'INV 10xx' + 12 x Bacs 'SumUp Payments Limited' 3000 -> 'FPS CREDIT OAKFIELD PROPERTIES' other; money in 84000, M2 0.0, M16 100.0.

findings.claim: When --opening-balance is given, the Monzo Balance column is ignored and never cross-checked, so a wrong opening balance yields a self-consistent statement with invented balances that ingest accepts; M5 and M6 are then wrong.
findings.repro: Export with Balance column (990.00, 970.00) converted with opening_balance=5000 -> balance_source 'opening balance supplied', output balances 4990.00/4970.00, closing 4970.0 vs Monzo's 970.00, no error.

findings.claim: Policy is evaluated on the rounded metric (M10 at 2dp, M4/M16 at 1dp), so values just under a threshold pass it: unrounded DSCR 1.24958 is stored as 1.25 and R2 gives refer instead of fail.
findings.repro: scratchpad/panel03/data-intensive/p4_round.py: M8 12000, M9 20995, M11 6000 -> unrounded 1.2495833, M10 1.25, R2 'refer' (rule is >= 1.25 on_fail fail).

findings.claim: The float balance check at exactly 0.01 tolerance accepts or rejects the same 1p discrepancy depending on binary rounding, and accepted 1p errors add up unchecked across lines.
findings.repro: rows (0.10 -> bal 0.10), (+0.20 -> bal 0.31) accepted; (+0.20 -> bal 0.29) rejected. 365 lines with amount 100.01 where the balance moves by 100.00: 182 lines rejected and 183 accepted (p8_tol.py).

findings.claim: Monzo Transaction IDs are replaced by positional ids M00001..., so evidence cannot be traced back to Monzo's own lines, and re-importing an export with one extra earlier row renumbers every id.
findings.repro: Read monzo.py:163: id=f'M{n:05d}' by sorted position; tid is not written to the output CSV (Monzo balance probe: mb.csv rows tx_1, tx_2 come out of convert() as M00001, M00002 in mb_out.csv).

findings.claim: LIST_MARKER blanks any number at the start of a line that is followed by '.' or ')', so a hard-wrapped figure such as '35. ' escapes the guard.
findings.repro: guard.check('Revenue was £<M2> [M2]. The owner expects\n35. More covers next year.', ...) -> grounded True.
